paper.title: A Layered Simplex Architecture for Large Alphabets

conventions.units: bits everywhere (regret, KL, codelength per token)
conventions.seeds: every experiment takes --seed and defaults to the fixed seed of the published run; identical seeds reproduce identical Monte-Carlo draws
conventions.procedure: all probabilities come from explicit formulas evaluated on count profiles (paper, Section 3.1); the only statistical error is the average over sampled profiles or trials
conventions.expected_values: expected/paper_values.json holds the paper's numbers for comparison
conventions.smoke_runs: every entry below lists a smoke variant that exercises the full code path in minutes at reduced scale
conventions.table_store: moment-table rows persist in the certified universal store at tables/universal_v2 (override with LSA_UNIVERSAL_TABLES); first use builds a row, every later experiment reuses it

results.description: One draw of the LSA prior at d = 24, L = 4
Online regret of every depth and of the depth average, vs Zipf exponent, at three alphabet sizes
commands: python scripts/depth_tilt_report.py --results output/fig2_d1e3/results.json output/fig2_d1e4/results.json output/fig2_d1e6/results.json --out output/fig2_report

results.description: Symbol discovery and the alphabet/data scaling tests on the Section 4.1 factorial grid at c = c*

results.description: Compressing the King James Bible over the fixed d = 100,000 vocabulary: the depth-averaged LSA predictor against the classical sequential coders
results.smoke: python scripts/unigram_experiment.py --corpus data/kjv.txt --d 100000 --checkpoints 10000 --jobs 2 --out output/table7_n10k  # ~4 min; reproduces row 1 of Table 7 (redundancy 1.052, mode L = 21)
results.runtime: baselines: seconds. LSA column: ~1 h on a modern multi-core machine for the first run; moment-table rows persist in the universal store (tables/universal_v2, gitignored), so later checkpoints and reruns are far faster

results.paper_item: Table 8 (LSA rows) and Section 5.4 in-text numbers
results.description: Order-one models of the Bible: per-state depth-averaged predictors over the M most frequent contexts plus backoff, averaged over the split-count grid
results.runtime: heavy (hundreds of per-state profiles at d = 10^5); run on a multi-core machine

results.description: Train a byte-pair vocabulary on the corpus itself and rerun the depth analysis: the stream flattens, the posterior collapses onto the shallowest depths, and all reasonable methods tie. The paper does not pin the vocabulary size; the claim is checked at three.
results.smoke: python scripts/bible_bpe_check.py --corpus data/kjv.txt --vocab-size 512 --checkpoints 20000,60000 --jobs 2 --out output/bpe_check_smoke  # ~3 min; already shows the tie and the shallow collapse
results.runtime: minutes per vocabulary size (small alphabet, shallow depths)

results.paper_item: Section 5.4 in-text online context-learning code (7.204 bits/token)
results.description: Fully sequential order-one code with no context-set header: a context is promoted to its own state once its count so far crosses a threshold; per-state depth-averaged predictors; uniform mixture over a threshold grid. The result is insensitive to the grid, the depth ceiling, and the promotion boundary (all three were varied).
results.runtime: ~40 min on 2 cores with a warm table store; the first run builds ~35k moment rows
